name: chest_pain_stemi_pathway

trigger.description: 62-year-old male presenting to ED with acute substernal chest pain radiating to left arm, onset 45 minutes ago. Diaphoretic, nauseous. History of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. Home medications: metformin 1000mg BID, lisinopril 20mg daily, atorvastatin 40mg daily.

expected_behavior: Full pipeline: triage with ESI-1/2, analyze cardiac enzymes and ECG, prescribe DAPT and anticoagulation, schedule cardiac catheterization, generate discharge summary.

reads.query: retrieve patient PAT-201 medical history including cardiac risk factors, prior ECGs, and current medications
patient PAT-201 allergy list and contraindications for antiplatelet and anticoagulation therapy
STEMI clinical pathway protocol and door-to-balloon time benchmarks
cardiac catheterization lab availability and on-call interventional cardiology schedule
prior cardiac emergency case outcomes for quality benchmarking

writes.content: Clinical assessment PAT-201: 62M presenting with acute STEMI. Troponin elevated, ST elevation in leads II, III, aVF. DAPT initiated (aspirin 325mg + clopidogrel 600mg loading). Heparin bolus administered.
Protocol adherence note: STEMI pathway activated for PAT-201. Door-to-ECG 8 minutes, door-to-activation 12 minutes. Target door-to-balloon <90 minutes.
Disposition: PAT-201 transferred to cardiac catheterization lab. Interventional cardiology team activated. All pre-procedure orders completed and verified.
Resource allocation: Cath lab 2 reserved for PAT-201 STEMI intervention. Estimated procedure duration 60-90 minutes. ICU bed reserved post-procedure.
Quality metric: STEMI bundle compliance for PAT-201 — door-to-balloon achieved within target. All core measures met. Case flagged for peer review as exemplar.

name: pneumonia_admission

trigger.description: 78-year-old female with 3-day history of productive cough, fever to 39.4C, and progressive dyspnea. CURB-65 score 3 (confusion, BUN >20, RR >30, age >65). Known COPD on home oxygen 2L. Current medications: tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol PRN.

expected_behavior: Full pipeline: triage ESI-2, analyze imaging and labs, prescribe IV antibiotics per CAP guidelines, schedule ICU bed, generate admission documentation.

reads.query: retrieve patient PAT-202 medical history including COPD severity, home oxygen settings, and prior pneumonia admissions
patient PAT-202 current medication list and antibiotic allergy history
community-acquired pneumonia treatment guidelines and CURB-65 score-based disposition criteria
ICU bed availability and respiratory therapy staffing for overnight shift
recent CAP admission outcomes and antibiotic stewardship metrics

writes.content: Clinical assessment PAT-202: 78F with severe CAP, CURB-65 score 3. CXR showing right lower lobe consolidation. Sputum and blood cultures obtained. IV ceftriaxone 2g + azithromycin 500mg initiated per CAP protocol.
Protocol adherence note: CAP bundle initiated for PAT-202. Blood cultures before antibiotics confirmed. Time to first antibiotic dose 45 minutes from ED arrival.
Disposition: PAT-202 admitted to ICU bed 12B. Respiratory therapy consulted for BiPAP evaluation. Pulmonology consult requested for COPD exacerbation management.
Resource allocation: ICU bed 12B assigned to PAT-202. Respiratory therapist allocated for q4h treatments. Isolation precautions pending culture results.
Quality metric: CAP bundle compliance for PAT-202 — blood cultures before antibiotics met, time-to-antibiotic within 60-minute target, appropriate severity-based disposition to ICU.

name: elective_knee_replacement

trigger.description: 55-year-old male scheduled for elective right total knee arthroplasty. Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritis refractory to conservative management including physical therapy, NSAIDs, and intra-articular injections. Pre-operative clearance pending. Medications: celecoxib 200mg daily, acetaminophen 1000mg TID, gabapentin 300mg TID.

expected_behavior: Full pipeline: triage ESI-5, analyze imaging (MRI knee), check drug interactions for peri-operative meds, schedule OR and pre-op labs, obtain insurance pre-auth, generate pre-op documentation.

patient PAT-203 comorbidities for pre-operative cardiac risk assessment and bleeding risk evaluation
total knee arthroplasty pre-operative protocol including medication hold guidelines for NSAIDs and anticoagulants

writes.content: Pre-operative assessment PAT-203: 55M cleared for right TKA. Cardiac risk low (revised cardiac risk index 0). Celecoxib held 7 days pre-op. No drug interactions with planned anesthesia regimen.
Protocol adherence note: TKA pre-op checklist completed for PAT-203. Labs (CBC, BMP, PT/INR, type and screen) ordered. Insurance pre-authorization obtained.

Resource allocation: OR-3 reserved for PAT-203 TKA, estimated 2 hours. Post-op bed on orthopedic floor confirmed. PT and OT consults pre-ordered.
Documentation: Pre-operative package for PAT-203 right TKA complete. All clearances obtained, consent signed, surgical site marked per protocol.

name: pediatric_asthma_exacerbation

trigger.description: 8-year-old male brought in by parents with acute asthma exacerbation. Wheezing, accessory muscle use, difficulty speaking in full sentences. Used albuterol inhaler 3 times at home without improvement. Known asthma (moderate persistent) since age 4. Current controller: fluticasone 110mcg BID. No prior intubations. Last ED visit for asthma 6 months ago.

expected_behavior: Full pipeline: triage ESI-2, analyze severity with peak flow and clinical assessment, prescribe continuous albuterol nebulization and systemic corticosteroids, monitor response, generate documentation with asthma action plan update.

reads.query: retrieve patient PAT-204 asthma history, controller medications, prior ED visits, and intubation history
patient PAT-204 weight-based dosing parameters and allergy list for pediatric bronchodilator and corticosteroid prescribing
pediatric asthma exacerbation severity scoring and treatment escalation protocol
pediatric respiratory therapy staffing and continuous nebulization equipment availability
pediatric asthma ED visit frequency and readmission rates for quality tracking

writes.content: Clinical assessment PAT-204: 8M with moderate-severe asthma exacerbation. Peak flow 45% predicted. Continuous albuterol nebulization initiated, dexamethasone 0.6mg/kg PO administered. Reassessment in 1 hour.
Protocol adherence note: Pediatric asthma pathway activated for PAT-204. Severity classified as moderate-severe per NAEPP guidelines. Weight-based dosing verified by pharmacist.
Treatment update: PAT-204 responding to continuous nebulization. SpO2 improved to 95%, respiratory rate decreased to 26. Plan to transition to intermittent treatments and observe 2 hours.
Resource tracking: Pediatric continuous nebulization station occupied for PAT-204. Respiratory therapist assigned for duration of continuous treatment.
Quality metric: Pediatric asthma bundle compliance for PAT-204 — severity assessment within 15 minutes, corticosteroids within 30 minutes, updated asthma action plan provided at discharge.

name: diabetic_ketoacidosis

trigger.description: 24-year-old female with type 1 diabetes presenting with nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and altered mental status. Blood glucose 485 mg/dL by fingerstick. Fruity breath odor noted. Reports missing insulin doses for 2 days due to pump malfunction. Last A1c 8.9%. Home regimen: insulin pump with Humalog.

expected_behavior: Full pipeline: triage ESI-1, analyze BMP/ABG/ketones, prescribe IV insulin drip and aggressive fluid resuscitation per DKA protocol, schedule ICU admission, file quality metric for DKA bundle compliance, generate discharge summary with diabetes education.

reads.query: retrieve patient PAT-205 diabetes history, insulin pump settings, last A1c, and prior DKA admissions
patient PAT-205 renal function history and electrolyte baselines for DKA management
DKA treatment protocol including insulin drip titration, fluid resuscitation rates, and potassium replacement thresholds
ICU bed availability and endocrinology on-call coverage for DKA management
DKA bundle compliance rates and average time to anion gap closure for benchmarking

writes.content: Clinical assessment PAT-205: 24F with DKA. Glucose 485, pH 7.18, bicarb 8, anion gap 28, large serum ketones. IV insulin drip at 0.1 units/kg/hr initiated. NS bolus 1L over 1 hour, then 500mL/hr. K+ 3.8 — replacement initiated before insulin.
Protocol adherence note: DKA pathway activated for PAT-205. Insulin drip protocol initiated with hourly glucose and q2h BMP monitoring. Target glucose reduction 50-75 mg/dL/hr.
Disposition: PAT-205 admitted to ICU bed 8A for DKA management. Endocrinology consult placed. Diabetes educator scheduled for day 2. Insulin pump manufacturer contacted for malfunction report.
Resource allocation: ICU bed 8A assigned to PAT-205. Insulin drip protocol requires 1:1 nursing. Endocrinology consult and diabetes education team notified.

Quality metric: DKA bundle compliance for PAT-205 — potassium checked before insulin, fluid resuscitation within 30 minutes, anion gap closure monitoring initiated. Discharge planning to include pump replacement and diabetes education.
